mission.title: Access lifecycle — joiners, movers, leavers
mission.system: Registre RH et habilitations (cycle de vie des accès)
mission.owner: IT department — IAM team; HR for the register
mission.lead_auditor: Attest CI (automated run, no human auditor)
scope_in: Reconciliation of the HR register with accounts at the reference date
Entitlements held by enabled accounts (segregation of duties, movers, privileges)
scope_out: Accuracy of the HR register itself

target_label: HR register ↔ entitlements (leavers, movers, conflicting rights)

control.title: Leaver account deactivation
control.objective: No person account with enabled=true has a linked employee with end_date earlier than as_of; end_date equal to as_of, in the future, or null is compliant and only enabled accounts are in scope.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve as_of from GET /api/lifecycle/meta, accounts from GET /api/lifecycle/accounts and employees from GET /api/hr/employees and flag any account with enabled=true and type=person whose linked employee has end_date < as_of.
control.expected: enabled=false for any person account where linked employee end_date < as_of; enabled=true allowed only if end_date is null or end_date >= as_of
control.risk: A former employee retains logical access and could read, modify or initiate unauthorized transactions after contract end.
control.recommendation: Disable the non-compliant leaver accounts immediately via the change management process and remove their entitlements.
control.cause: The HR leaver feed is likely not interfaced automatically to the access deprovisioning process or manual deactivation was delayed.

before.expected: enabled=false for any person account where linked employee end_date < as_of; enabled=true allowed only if end_date is null or end_date >= as_of
before.detail: Checked 859 enabled person accounts out of 932 total accounts and 920 employees at as_of 2026-11-02 with no enabled account having end_date before as_of

inspection.comment: The page shows account status at as_of 2026-11-02 but contains no employee end_date column to verify leaver deactivation.

control.title: Account ownership linkage
control.objective: Every account with enabled=true is linked to a known responsible person present in the HR register, meaning person accounts have employee_id existing in employees and service accounts have owner_employee_id existing in employees with an active employee.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve accounts from GET /api/lifecycle/accounts and employees from GET /api/hr/employees and flag any account with enabled=true where employee_id for type=person or owner_employee_id for type=service is missing from employees or refers to a left employee.
control.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true, employee_id (type=person) or owner_employee_id (type=service) exists in employee_id and linked status=active
control.risk: Orphan or ownerless accounts cannot be attributed or approved and could be abused without detection or accountability.
control.recommendation: Attach each orphan account to a known active responsible or disable and delete it following the change management process.
control.cause: Account creation likely allows manual entry of identifiers without referential check against the HR register or owner departure does not trigger service account review.

before.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true, employee_id (type=person) or owner_employee_id (type=service) exists in employee_id and linked status=active
before.detail: Checked 623 enabled accounts against 380 employees: all linked to active employees.

inspection.comment: All visible enabled accounts on page 1 include a matricule value with no empty linkage field.

control.title: Dormant person accounts
control.objective: No person account with enabled=true has been inactive for more than 90 days measured as as_of minus last_login, or as_of minus created if last_login is null, with exactly 90 days compliant and service accounts out of scope.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve as_of from GET /api/lifecycle/meta and accounts from GET /api/lifecycle/accounts and flag any account with enabled=true and type=person where as_of minus last_login or created if last_login is null exceeds 90 days.
control.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true and type=person, (as_of - last_login or as_of - created if last_login=null) <= 90 days
control.risk: Unused dormant accounts can be hijacked to gain persistent undetected access to banking data and functions.
control.recommendation: Disable or recertify dormant person accounts after verification with managers via the change management process.
control.cause: Periodic inactivity monitoring and automatic disabling after prolonged non-use is likely missing or misconfigured.

before.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true and type=person, (as_of - last_login or as_of - created if last_login=null) <= 90 days
before.detail: Checked 383 accounts (355 enabled person) with as_of 2026-11-02, found 0 dormant over 90 days.

inspection.comment: Page 1 of 4 shows as_of 2026-11-02 with all visible active accounts having last login within 60 days.

control.title: Segregation of duties
control.objective: No account with enabled=true holds both entitlements paiements.saisie and paiements.validation together, nor both credit.instruction and credit.decision together.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve accounts from GET /api/lifecycle/accounts and flag any account with enabled=true whose entitlements list contains both conflicting pairs.
control.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true, entitlements does not contain (paiements.saisie + paiements.validation) nor (credit.instruction + credit.decision)
control.risk: A single user could initiate and approve the same payment or credit decision, enabling fraud and undetected errors.
control.recommendation: Remove one of the conflicting entitlements from each violating account via the change management process.
control.cause: Entitlement assignment likely lacks preventive SoD conflict checks at provisioning time.

before.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true, entitlements does not contain (paiements.saisie + paiements.validation) nor (credit.instruction + credit.decision)
before.detail: Checked 358 enabled accounts among 383 total accounts, found 0 violations.

inspection.comment: Page 1 of 4 shows 100 accounts with no enabled account holding both conflicting entitlements.

control.title: Mover rights removal
control.objective: No account with enabled=true retains an entitlement whose department equals the holder previous_department more than 30 days after transfer_date, with exactly 30 days compliant and entitlements with department=null out of scope.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve as_of from GET /api/lifecycle/meta, accounts from GET /api/lifecycle/accounts, employees from GET /api/hr/employees and entitlements from GET /api/lifecycle/entitlements and flag any enabled account holding an entitlement with department equal to previous_department where as_of minus transfer_date exceeds 30 days.
control.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true, no entitlements with department == previous_department when (as_of - transfer_date) > 30 days; department=null always allowed
control.risk: Transferred employees accumulate excessive rights from former and new departments, allowing unauthorized actions beyond their current role.
control.recommendation: Remove former-department entitlements retained beyond 30 days after transfer via the change management process.
control.cause: The mover process likely copies new rights without automatically revoking old department rights after the 30-day grace period.

before.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true, no entitlements with department == previous_department when (as_of - transfer_date) > 30 days; department=null always allowed
before.detail: Checked 383 accounts (358 enabled) against 380 employees at as_of 2026-11-02, finding 0 enabled mover accounts retaining previous-department entitlements beyond 30 days

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows only account status and rights without transfer dates or previous departments needed to verify mover rule.

control.title: Privileged access review
control.objective: Every account with enabled=true holding at least one privileged entitlement has last_access_review not null and within 365 days before or on as_of.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve as_of from GET /api/lifecycle/meta, accounts from GET /api/lifecycle/accounts and entitlements from GET /api/lifecycle/entitlements and flag any enabled account whose entitlements include a privileged=true entitlement but whose last_access_review is null or older than 365 days from as_of.
control.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true where entitlements includes privileged=true, last_access_review != null and (as_of - last_access_review) <= 365 days
control.risk: Unreviewed privileged rights persist beyond business need and could be exploited to compromise critical ICT assets.
control.recommendation: Perform an immediate access review of flagged privileged accounts and remove unjustified rights via the change management process.
control.cause: The annual privileged access recertification campaign likely misses some accounts due to incomplete scoping or follow-up.

before.expected: for all accounts with enabled=true where entitlements includes privileged=true, last_access_review != null and (as_of - last_access_review) <= 365 days
before.detail: Checked 7 enabled privileged accounts out of 383 total accounts against as_of 2026-11-02 with no overdue review.
